title: lefagy, újraindít, frissít: When the Computer Misbehaves

sections.title: Four words for a bad day online
sections.content: Technology goes wrong in a few predictable ways, and Hungarian has one word for each. *lefagy* means "to freeze, to crash", *újraindít* "to restart", *frissít* "to update" and *hiba* "error, fault". You know *hibás* ("faulty") from Unit 16 and *elromlik* ("to break down") from Unit 15; the new words say exactly what broke. *számítógép* ("computer") is the thing that most often freezes. In *újraindít* the word *újra* ("again") sits in front of *indít* ("to start") in the same place as *fel-* or *le-*.

sections.title: Key phrases
rows: There is an error in the app.

items.spanish: Újraindítom a telefont, aztán frissítem az alkalmazást.
items.english: I restart the phone, then I update the app.

sections.content: *hiba* is a noun and *hibás* an adjective. Say *hiba van az alkalmazásban* ("there is an error in the app") but *hibás az alkalmazás* ("the app is faulty").
